examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Slope of the Tangent Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form at a Point
examples.problem: Find the slope of the tangent at the point $\left(1,\,2 \right)$ for the curve $xy+y^2=2x^2+4.$
examples.worked_solution:
To find the slope at a point, we use implicit differentiation to calculate the derivative of the curve, assuming that $y = y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the $xy$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(xy+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}+4) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(xy)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}+4) \\ x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4x \\ x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4x \\ (x+2y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4x-y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{4x-y}{x+2y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at the point $\left(1,\,2 \right)$ is given by

$$
\eqalign{
m
&=\left(\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}\right)_{\left(1,\,2 \right)}\[5pt]
&=\left(\dfrac{4x-y}{x+2y}\right)_{\left(1,\,2 \right)}\[5pt]
&=\dfrac{4\cdot 1-2}{1+2\cdot 2}\[5pt]
&=\dfrac{2}{5} \, .
}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

 Note that to differentiate the ${x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)+4{y}^{4}=6{x}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)+4{y}^{4}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y))+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{y}^{4}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{x}^{3}) \\ [{x}^{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)]+16{y}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =18{x}^{2} \\ -{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)+16{y}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =18{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+16{y}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =18{x}^{2}-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(16{y}^{3}-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)) & =18{x}^{2}-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{18{x}^{2}-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)}{16{y}^{3}-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)}\end{aligned}
$$
